tiles.name: pi pad
tiles.subtitle: -20 dB
notes: A pi attenuator: 61.9 / 249 / 61.9 ohm is -20.0 dB and 50.0 ohm in a 50 ohm system (6.12's $10 pad, on the board).
Into a high-impedance load it is only -14 dB: the pad assumes 50 ohm on both sides.

tiles.name: RC low-pass
tiles.subtitle: 159 kHz
tiles.result: -3 dB at 159 kHz, then -20 dB/decade; OUT into the ADC's high impedance
notes: 1 k and 1 nF: f = 1 / (2 pi R C) = 159 kHz.  Measure OUT with the ADC on its high-impedance setting: a 50 ohm
load would make a 1 k / 50 divider of it.  The lag plant of 4.08 and 7.06; the step response is 1 - exp(-t / 1 us).

tiles.name: RC high-pass
tiles.subtitle: 159 kHz
tiles.result: -3 dB at 159 kHz, +20 dB/decade below; OUT into high impedance
notes: The mirror image of P2: the same 1 k and 1 nF the other way round.  A step in gives a spike that decays in 1 us.

tiles.name: series RLC
tiles.subtitle: 100uH 220pF
tiles.result: a peak at 1.07 MHz (switches off), 0.98 with 1, 0.89 with 2, 0.83 with both; Q about 6
notes: Series L C between 50 ohm ports: a band-pass at f = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) whose Q = sqrt(L/C) / (100 + R_coil) is about 6
(the 10 ohm coil would give 60 by itself).  The DIP switch adds 47 pF (way 1) and 100 pF (way 2) across the 220 pF to move
the peak; a resonant plant for 7.06, a lockbox's cavity before the real one.  No OUT loop (the switch took its corner).

tiles.name: LC low-pass
tiles.subtitle: 9 MHz
tiles.result: -3 dB at 8.9 MHz, -30 dB at 18 MHz: the anti-alias filter in front of a 25 MS/s ADC
notes: 5th-order Butterworth, 50 ohm: 220 pF, 1.5 uH, 680 pF, 1.5 uH, 220 pF (the exact values are 219 pF, 1.43 uH, 707 pF).
Before the ADC it removes 6.10's ghost; after the DAC it smooths the steps.

tiles.name: LC low-pass
tiles.subtitle: 100 kHz
tiles.result: -3 dB at 118 kHz: the reconstruction filter after a one-bit DAC
notes: 3rd-order pi, 50 ohm: 2 x 10 nF, 150 uH, 2 x 10 nF, all C0G (JLCPCB stocks no 22 nF C0G in 0805 or 1206).
Turns 7.05's one-bit stream into a tone; the slow plant of 7.06 with P2.

tiles.name: band-pass
tiles.subtitle: 4.7-7.5 MHz
tiles.result: Chapter 6's band: a peak at 6.3 MHz, 3 dB from 4.7 to 7.5 MHz
notes: 3rd-order Butterworth band-pass, 6.05 MHz centre, 3.1 MHz wide: series 2.7 uH + 270 pF, shunt 330 nH || 2.2 nF, series 2.7 uH + 270 pF
(the exact values: 2.57 uH, 269 pF, 337 nH, 2.05 nF).  6.10's filtered chips in copper; the transmitter's harmonics and the
receiver's front end of 5.07 and 6.12.

tiles.name: quartz crystal
tiles.subtitle: 4 MHz
tiles.result: a sharp pass at the series resonance near 4.000 MHz (-3.7 dB) and a notch 6.0 kHz above it, the parallel resonance
notes: The crystal in series between 50 ohm ports: it passes at its series resonance f_s (R_m about 50 ohm: -3.5 dB) and blocks at
the parallel resonance f_p = f_s (1 + C_m / 2 C_0) a few kHz above.  A capacitor across OUT (a tee at the ADC) pulls f_p
down toward f_s and leaves f_s alone: the pulling that 4.09 measures.  Model: C_m 15 fF, Q 50 000, C_0 4 pF (typical HC-49S).

tiles.name: ceramic res.
tiles.subtitle: 455 kHz
tiles.result: a pass near 455 kHz and a notch a few kHz above: a resonator with a Q of a few hundred, between P4's LC and P8's quartz
notes: A two-terminal 455 kHz ceramic resonator in series (JLCPCB stocks no three-terminal 455 kHz filter).  It is the superhet's IF
element, and here a resonance whose Q (hundreds) sits between the LC's and the crystal's.  Model: C_m 7 pF, Q 400, C_0 250 pF.

tiles.name: clipper
tiles.subtitle: 1N4148 ±0.6 V
tiles.result: a sine of more than 1 V comes out flat-topped at about ±0.6 V; the ADC on high impedance
notes: 1 k in series, then a 1N4148W each way to ground: whatever goes in, OUT stays within a diode drop.  4.04's harmonics: the
clipped sine's spectrum against the amplitude; the 1 k limits the diode current to a few milliamps from a ±4 V source.

tiles.name: delay line
tiles.subtitle: 400 ns, a tap every 100
tiles.result: a pulse arrives at OUT 395 ns late, at the taps every 99 ns; flat to about 10 MHz, then it disperses
notes: Twenty sections of 1.0 uH and 390 pF: Z0 = sqrt(L/C) = 51 ohm, 20 ns a section, cut-off 1 / (pi sqrt(LC)) = 16 MHz.
400 ns is 260 ft of RG-58.  Leave OUT open and a pulse comes back the same way up; short it and it comes back inverted;
50 ohm on OUT and nothing comes back (4.05).  The taps are 6.05's echo and 6.10's radar target; near 16 MHz the
phase velocity falls and a chirp spreads (7.06's pure-delay plant below that).  A tap through 470 ohm: x1 into a
high-impedance scope, /10 into 50 ohm.
texts: 20 ns a section, taps via 470 ohm

tiles.name: LEDs
tiles.result: one LED at a time; the voltage where it starts to glow against 1/wavelength is h/e
notes: 100 ohm from the jack to the four LEDs; the 4-way switch picks one.  Drive from the DAC through the ECP5 board's unipolar
LED output or a bench supply: the knee voltage of each colour against c / lambda gives Planck's constant (4.10).
Way 1 red 630 nm (AlGaInP), 2 yellow 596 (AlGaInP), 3 green 525 (InGaN), 4 blue 469 nm (InGaN): the InGaN pair lie
above the line.  The LED loop is after the 100 ohm: the LED's own voltage.  The colours are not on the silk: light them.

tiles.name: AM loopstick
tiles.subtitle: 0.5-1.7 MHz
tiles.result: with a 330 uH loopstick: 1.28 MHz on 1, 0.88 on 2, 0.59 on 3, 0.40 MHz on 4, and the sums between (the AM band)
notes: Any ferrite-rod AM antenna coil (about 330 uH; 50 to 100 mm long) screws into the terminal, its tap (a quarter of the turns
from the ground end) to the jack.  The switch's capacitors tune it: f = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)), 1.28 MHz with 47 pF down to
0.40 MHz with 470 pF; combine positions for the steps between.  Into A4's LNA and 1.10's AM radio: a real station.

back_text: AMOD-P: passive building blocks for the FPGA tutorial's converters.  Each tile is one circuit with its own SMA jacks:
cable DAC OUT to a tile's IN and its OUT to ADC IN.  Every jack takes +-4 V.  No power.  The handbook has each tile's
expected response.  P13 wants a ferrite-rod coil (about 330 uH) along this edge, under cable ties through the slots.
